install-overwrite-aborted: The TS abort handler removed installSubDir, which on an update is the EXISTING install, so aborting an update deleted the installed version while the store still said isInstalled (87-07 finding 2). The Rust install touches the existing directory only after the whole archive is downloaded and its checksum has passed, so an abort leaves the installed version and its store entry as they were. Only the tree differs from the golden.
install-overwrite-unzip-throws: The TS restore branch tested error.includes('AbortError') on an Error object, which throws a TypeError before the backup is renamed back, so a failed extraction left the old tree as <dir>_backup beside a half-made install and the archive (87-07 finding 1). The Rust install removes the half-made directory through gamelib-safety and renames the backup back, and removes the archive. Result, notifications, events, requests and store are the golden's; only the tree differs.
install-tar-nonzero-swallowed: The TS extractFiles reports { status: 'error' } for a non-zero tar exit instead of throwing, so the install carried on, measured an empty directory and told the user it had finished (87-07 finding 3). The Rust install stops on a failed tar: the install directory is removed (and a backup restored), nothing is stored, no wineVersionsUpdated is pushed, the notification is the error one and du is never run. Everything up to and including the tar spawn is the golden's.
